deviations_from_the_spec: The scripts do not exist yet (only guard-hook.mjs and selftest.mjs are in tcb/scripts), so the tests have never run against the real scripts. All three files pass node --check. I ran them far enough to see each reach the child-process spawn and fail only because the script file is missing. Along the way I confirmed that fsck's baseline root builds (git init and commit work), that a junction can be created, that a test-owned sleeper's start time reads back in the 7-digit Z form, and that the git config hazard of fsck T17 is live without hardening (the marker was created).

Every test builds its root itself with fs.mkdtempSync under tcb-build/tmp, using prefixes tcbcm-, tcbhv- and tcbfs-. The tests do not import lib.mjs or tcb/test/helpers.mjs. canonicalize, sha256, objectId, ledger hashing and verification, transcript writing and the lock holder are small independent copies inside each test file, so the tests do not trust the library they indirectly check. The same block of helper code appears in all three files, between COMMON HELPERS BEGIN and END.

Fixtures are flat files named _*.json and _agent-reader.md directly under tcb/fixtures/<script>/, not case folders. They are not selftest case.json cases, which the script builders write. Run roots, rows, ledger lines, manifests and transcripts are built in code from these few synthetic cards.

Beyond the numbered behaviours I added tests named X<n>, one per spec sentence that no T covers. Commit: X1 (no transcript, exit 2), X2 (step-not-listed), X3 (pack-count), X4 (no-outputs). Harvest: X1 (zero candidates exit 0, and result.foreign). Fsck: X1 (no coord.json, exit 2 no-coordinator).

Some tests assert slightly more than the T line states, taken from the spec's step text. Commit T7 adds a resolvable supersession (accepted) and a supersede_reason without supersedes (rejected). Commit T22 adds a confirmed card that is superseded by a pack card (not cut). Commit T23 adds the no-frozen-protocol case. Fsck T12 adds settings-missing and a nested .claude folder. Fsck T16 adds a missing cut file.

Fsck T13 (an intake line appended between phase 1 and phase 2) cannot be forced into the window, because the spec names no file or stderr signal at the end of phase 1. The test plays the other writer. It holds run.lock with a test-owned sleeper, waits about 4 s (a timer used only to raise the odds of overlap, never to decide the outcome), appends an intake line naming a non-canonical object, then releases the lock. The asserted outcome (exit 3, object-mismatch in failing) is the same whether the line lands before or after phase 1 read the head, so the phase-2-only path is not proven.

Commit T14 expects a repeated `record` on a row that is already `committed` to exit 0. Commit spec step 2 says record starts as intake does, and intake answers 65 wrong-step for a row that is not active at started or bound. I followed T14 and CONTRACT 3.6 (a committed row stays at step bound, repeats are idempotent). If the builder reads step 2 literally, T14 will fail, and the spec needs one clarifying sentence.

Commit T19 deletes the staged files before altering the stored object. Otherwise the intake pass that record runs would hit id-collision (also exit 3) at step 3 instead of object-mismatch at step 7. The staging files that the stale-object tampering leaves behind would give a different code.

Where the contract marks a row or attempt field with '?', the fixtures leave the field out rather than writing null (reason, bound_at, boot, cut and spend_at_fence are omitted). The tasks schema has not been written yet. If it requires nullable fields to be present, every test fails with exit 67 at once, so check that first.

Transcript records use the Claude Code shape (type assistant/user/attachment, sessionId, cwd, message.id, message.model, usage fields, tool_use and tool_result blocks, attachment.type structured_output with data). The helpers.fakeTranscript signature was not used because its tools, results and structured shapes are not pinned and I needed to control tool ids for the Agent result in harvest T2.

Shapes the contract leaves open, assumed as follows. attempts[].folder is a root-relative posix path (wt/<task>-e<e>). The protocol-freeze ledger line carries path as root-relative posix (plan/frozen/protocol-<field>-<sha12>.json). The cut line carries data.sha as the full sha256 of the cut file. A rejected entry's file is posix and relative to the attempt folder (staging/cards/x.card.json), as CONTRACT 3.22 says. For fsck, a failing item's id is the object id (without .json), the ledger break position as a string, and for a commit mismatch only check and code are asserted. The ledger lines I write carry ce 1, writer and writer_sha zeros.
lib_change_requests: tcb/thresholds.json as shipped in tcb-build/tcb lacks names the contract table lists and the scripts will read (lock_retries, proc_exe, user_files, hook_deadline_ms, selftest_case_ms, sleep_gap_ms, fetch_max_redirects and others). My tests write their own full thresholds.json into each temp root, so they do not depend on the shipped file. U5c should still complete it to the CONTRACT 3.20 table.
CONTRACT 3.12 and 3.6 leave open whether `commit record` on a row already `committed` goes through the active/bound check of intake. Please state it in spec/commit.mjs.md (see the T14 deviation).

CONTRACT 3.18 names `path` in the protocol-freeze ledger line without saying root-relative or absolute. fsck, commit (lib.currentProtocol) and protocol-freeze must agree. Please add one word to the contract.
not_testable_without_the_app: commit N1 (spec 'Needs the app'): a real reader's URLs appear in the child's or helper's transcript in the 4.8 shape (CONTRACT 7 item 7). Written as a skipped test with reason 'needs the app'.

harvest N1: a real reader's schema-checked result appears as a StructuredOutput input or structured_output attachment in its helper transcript, and helper transcripts lie below <session>/subagents/ (CONTRACT 7 item 7). Skipped, 'needs the app'.
harvest N2: the harness's schema retry of a helper result (CONTRACT 7 item 8). Skipped, 'needs the app'.
fsck: the spec lists no needs-app behaviour. Whether a real session obeys the settings fsck guards is item 3 and belongs to selftest.
open_points: fsck T13 is written, but it only proves that an intake line naming a corrupted object ends in exit 3. It cannot show that the phase-2 re-check of objects named after the head H1 does the work, because phase 1 also lists every object file. A deterministic check needs a seam (a stderr line or a file at the end of phase 1) that the spec does not give. This is the one numbered behaviour I could not turn into a deterministic test.

Commit behaviours without a numbered T that I did not test. wrong-field and question-not-owned (step 5). fk-card, fk-parent, index-invalid, dup-sid, bad-sid and dismissal cites outside the pack (step 6). unknown-kind and name-kind. The `ignored` list of non-JSON files. The checkpoint origin (in/checkpoint/** files and a junction there). A zombie-write or 65 on `record` (T10 covers intake only), wrong-step 65, and id-collision exit 3. record-side review-count and pack-not-frozen. The 'unparseable tasks.json' case for record.

Fsck behaviours without a numbered T that I did not test. fk-missing for certificate fields and for supersedes, parent and read_set targets. object-unlogged for `x_` and `m_` objects. The torn-tail anomaly. attempt-gone. A committed row missing a step as commit-mismatch. A frozen file named by protocol-amend or plan-freeze lines. The tcb check's timeout and git-not-found paths (no-git beyond a missing .git).

Harvest behaviours without a numbered T that I did not test. The wrong-step 65 (row not active at started or bound). That the script reads transcripts outside the lock. The `transcripts` count in the result, because the spec does not say whether it counts the main transcript. For T3 I did not assert `candidates`, because a reader result may count as one candidate or as two cards.

Any test that depends on the unwritten schemas (card, pack, review, commit-record, tasks) will show a failure in my row, card or pack fixtures as soon as the schemas differ from CONTRACT 3.1-3.6. First fixture to suspect: the card `date` field, the manifest fields (schema_version, brief_sha) and the row fields. The fixtures follow the contract tables literally.

Run time is dominated by the real process list: every script call starts PowerShell once (about 2 s on this machine). Contract 4.11 requires sequential tests for that reason, so I set no test concurrency. The three files can run in parallel as separate processes (`node --test --test-concurrency=3 tcb/test/commit.test.mjs tcb/test/harvest.test.mjs tcb/test/fsck.test.mjs`). Expect a few minutes for the whole set, mostly from fsck, which runs git and builds a repository per root.
Junction tests (commit T9, T25; harvest T11) skip themselves if a junction cannot be created. Tests that need git (all of fsck except T11 and X1; commit T20) skip when git is not installed.
